background_notes.fact: For 0<a≤1, the natural ceiling N=ceil(1/a) is finite and satisfies N≥1, 1/N≤a and N≤1/a+1≤2/a. The N closed intervals [j/N,(j+1)/N], 0≤j<N, cover [0,1] and have diameter 1/N.

grounds.reason: F001 supplies 0<a_i≤r for the chosen budgets.

background_notes.justification: The Archimedean property of the reals gives the least natural integer N≥1/a; its minimality gives N<1/a+1. Positivity permits reciprocation to obtain 1/N≤a. Adjacent interval endpoints agree, their first endpoint is zero and last is one, so their finite union is [0,1]. Distances in each interval are at most its endpoint difference, attained by its endpoints.

background_notes.fact: If ediam U≤ofReal a with finite a≥0 and J is a real interval of length b≤a, then ediam(U×J)≤ofReal a in MaxProd X. This also holds when U is empty.

grounds.reason: The selected pair supplies ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i and a_i>0.
Extended diameter is the supremum of pairwise extended distances.
The product distance is the maximum of the two component distances.

background_notes.justification: Every pair from U has distance ≤a by the diameter bound and the order-preserving embedding of nonnegative finite reals. Every pair from J has distance ≤b≤a. Hence each product distance, their maximum, is ≤a, and taking its supremum preserves the upper bound. An empty product has diameter zero.

background_notes.fact: For p>0 the extended nonnegative power x↦x^p is increasing. For finite a>0, (ofReal a)^p=ofReal(a^p), and for q>0 one has a^(q+1)=a*a^q. Consequently, N finite product sets each of diameter ≤ofReal a have total p-cost ≤ofReal(N*a^p), including empty sets when p>0.

grounds.reason: The chosen budgets are strictly positive finite reals.
The product diameter bounds and finite positive integers N_i have been established.
Real powers use exp(p log a) on positive bases and zero at base zero for positive exponents.

background_notes.justification: Monotonicity of log and exp proves power monotonicity for positive finite bases; the specified zero and infinity values give the endpoints. The exponential addition law gives a^(q+1)=a*a^q. Embedding nonnegative finite values commutes with these powers and finite sums. Bounding each of N costs and summing gives the stated inequality; empty-set cost is zero.

background_notes.fact: For finite natural N_i≥1, the set T={(i,j):i∈ℕ,j<N_i} has a natural enumeration without repetitions. For nonnegative extended costs c_(i,j), enumeration preserves the total sum and Σ_T c=Σ_i Σ_(j<N_i)c_(i,j). Nonnegative sums preserve termwise inequalities and commute with multiplication by a finite positive constant, in particular 2.

grounds.reason: Each N_i is a finite positive natural; all product costs and comparison terms lie in [0,∞].
Cover costs are nonnegative extended sums over natural indices.

background_notes.justification: List pairs in successive finite diagonals of ℕ×ℕ and retain exactly those in T. Every admissible pair occurs once; the pairs (i,0) show that the retained list is infinite. A nonnegative sum is the supremum of its finite subsums, so a bijection preserves it. Every finite set of pairs is contained in finitely many complete finite rows; conversely such rows form a finite set of pairs. This gives the regrouping identity. Termwise comparison follows on finite subsums. Multiplication by a fixed positive finite constant is an order isomorphism of [0,∞], hence preserves their suprema and gives the scaling identity.

background_notes.fact: If z∈[0,∞] satisfies z≤ofReal(2ε) for every real ε>0, then z=0.

grounds.reason: F002 supplies a cover of cost <ofReal(2ε) for every positive ε at the fixed positive scale.
N101 identifies the relevant content with the infimum of these cover costs.

background_notes.justification: Choosing ε=1 bounds z by the finite value 2, excluding infinity. If its finite real value t were positive, ε=t/4 would give t≤t/2, a contradiction. Nonnegativity therefore forces z=0. The subsequent supremum is a supremum of zero contents by N101, without any exchange of limits or integrals.
